item.text: I’ll inspect the repository’s database backends and existing tests, write the required checkpoint first, then implement the bulk operation in both backends and run the relevant existing tests.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "find .. -name AGENTS.md -o -name package.json -o -path '*database/mongo/hash.js' -o -path '*database/redis/hash.js' | head -200 && mkdir -p .codex-role-output && cat > .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'
# Checkpoint

Task: implement "'`incrObjectFieldByBulk` in Mongo and Redis hash backends with input validation, atomic per-key increments, upsert/missing-field behavior, and cache invalidation. Inspect existing backend patterns and tests, make the implementation, then run relevant existing tests.
EOF
ls -la'

item.text: Both backend methods are in place. Mongo issues one atomic `$inc` update per object; Redis uses a per-object atomic script that validates every current field before issuing any increments. Both validate the full request before database access and invalidate only keys whose writes succeeded. I’m running the existing hash test and lint checks now.

item.text:
Implemented `incrObjectFieldByBulk` in both [Mongo hash.js](/app/src/database/mongo/hash.js) and [Redis hash.js](/app/src/database/redis/hash.js). The methods validate input and safe integer increments, apply each object’s changes atomically, continue processing other objects after a key-level failure, and invalidate cache only for successful writes. Empty inputs perform no database or cache calls.

Verification: `test/database/hash.js` passed (64 tests) with a temporary local Redis server. ESLint and `git diff --check` passed.
